target_customer: SaaS, payments and financial-services companies (lenders, invoice-financing, expense-management and AP/AR tools) that need their business customers' accounting, commerce and payments data
problem: Fintech and SaaS builders must write and maintain separate integrations to many accounting, e-commerce and payments platforms to read their customers' financial data.
business_model: usage/subscription-based unified API (B2B developer API); exact pricing not found
product_category: unified API for business financial data (accounting, commerce, payments integrations)

founders.name: Ishwar Gogineni
education: University of Southern California, BSc Mathematics and Finance
founders.background_notes: YC page says he later led product at Commenda after the acquisition.

founders.background_notes: No bio details on YC page.

founders.background_notes: No bio details on YC page.

competitors.funding_then: reported $27M Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz in March 2022 (per a Merge comparison page, not independently checked)

technical_complexity.rationale: Normalising data across 30+ accounting, payments and e-commerce platforms (the company's own claim) is standard integration engineering but laborious; the hard part is breadth and upkeep, not research.

defensibility.rationale: Customers integrate once against the API, giving some lock-in, but rivals with far more funding offered the same wedge and each integration can be rebuilt.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Well-funded unified-API players (Rutter, Codat, Merge) already served the same need. Integration Labs was instead acquired by Commenda, its first customer; YC page says 2025.

market_need_then: Lenders, invoice-financing and expense-management fintechs needed programmatic access to SMEs' accounting data; the existence of funded unified-API vendors in 2022 (Rutter, Codat) shows active demand.
outcome_analysis: Integration Labs (formerly RootFi) raised a roughly $1.5M seed from YC and angels, built a unified financial-data API with 30+ integrations, and was eventually acquired by its first customer, Commenda, which says the product and team continue. The deal price is undisclosed and the YC directory marks the company Inactive, so it reads as a small, quiet exit in a market crowded with better-funded rivals rather than a clear success or failure.
notes: Seed date is conflicting (Dealroom says May 2023; Inc42 ties it to the 2022 YC cohort); amount stated as about $1.5M, one aggregator says $1.63M across 2 rounds. Acquisition date is from the YC page (2025); Commenda post shows only a 2026 last-updated date and no deal terms. Competitor figures come from a competitor's comparison page via search summary and were not verified against primary announcements. Company was formerly called RootFi. Directory status is Inactive but Commenda says the product continues under it, so the Inactive label likely reflects the acquisition (company absorbed), not a shutdown.
